To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a Bayesian approach can be used to improve gene clustering results when prior knowledge is available; (2) this approach is based on a mixture model whose parameters are constrained by a new type of prior distribution that can express the temporal nature of microarray data; and (3) the parameters of this model can be estimated with an EM algorithm that maximizes its posterior probability.
the use of prior knowledge about the temporal profile of classes of interests improves the clustering result and that the proposed method can handle both time series and time course data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods for the clustering and classification of gene expression time series.

the development of new statistical tools and methods that will allow the identification of genes with a specific function or a particular role in a given process, and the identification of genes involved in the regulation of other genes.

the proposed method can be successfully used for clustering gene expression data.
the results obtained by using the proposed method are better than those obtained using the classical clustering method.
